rich_summary: This chapter depicts the climactic struggle of the tenth day of the Kurukshetra war, when the invincible grandsire Bhishma devastates the Pandava forces. His slaughter is immense—thousands of warriors, elephants, and horses fall as he fights like a blazing cosmic fire, unmoved even when surrounded and pierced from every side. Krishna urges Arjuna to confront him directly, and the Pandava heroes rally together. Knowing Bhishma will not fight Sikhandin due to the latter’s past femininity, Arjuna places Sikhandin before him as a shield. While many warriors attack Bhishma, Arjuna repeatedly cuts down his weapons and showers him with arrows. Meanwhile Bhishma realizes the destined moment of his fall has come, remembering his boon of choosing the time of his death. Celestial beings approve his resolve, signaling the turning point when the greatest Kaurava champion prepares to yield to fate.

highlight_spans.why: Opening account of Bhishma’s staggering battlefield slaughter, establishing his near-superhuman dominance.
Description of Bhishma as a cosmic fire in battle, a powerful metaphor emphasizing his destructive, mythic presence.
Bhishma’s internal reflection on fate and his decision to accept death, marking the emotional and philosophical turning point.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma stands alone amid the battlefield like a blazing fire, arrows streaming from his bow while thousands of warriors surround him.
Arjuna on his chariot with Krishna as charioteer places Sikhandin before him and releases a storm of arrows toward the towering Bhishma.
Celestial sages and Vasus watch from the sky as flowers fall and Bhishma resolves within himself to choose the moment of his own death.
